introduction.p: Suppose that you are driving a car on the highway using cruise control so that you drive at a constant speed. The time, T (measured in hours), it takes to drive 50 miles depends on the constant rate, s (measured in miles per hour) at which you are driving. Since
and thus we know that T(s) = \frac{50}{s}\text{.}

For instance, observe that T(75) = \frac{50}{75} = \frac{2}{3}\text{,} so it takes \frac{2}{3} of an hour to drive 50 miles at 75 miles per hour, and the point (75, \frac{2}{3}) lies on the graph of T(s)\text{.}

statement.p: Give three points which lie on the graph of T\text{,} separated by commas.
Which of the following statements is true about the graph of T(s)\text{?}

li.p: The function is increasing because as speed goes up, travel time goes up.
The function is decreasing and decreasing more quickly, because the travel time decreases as speed increases, and it does so in a way that the decreases get larger.
The function is decreasing but decreasing more slowly, because the travel time decreases as speed increases, but the amount of decrease is getting smaller.

statement.p: What is the value of T(60)\text{?}
Which of the following is the best explanation of the meaning of this value in context?

li.p: T(60) is the time in hours it takes to travel 50 miles at a speed of 60 mph.
T(60) is how fast the travel time is changing when the car is traveling at a speed of 60 mph.

statement.p: Recall the average rate of change of a function f(x) on an interval [a,b] is
Determine the average rate of T on the interval [60,65]\text{,} AV_{[60, 65]}\text{.}

The sign of AV_{[60, 65]} is
positive
negative

li.p: T is increasing from 60 to 65 mph.
T is decreasing from 60 to 65 mph.
T is increasing but the amount of increase is smaller from 60 to 65 mph.
T is decreasing and the amount of decrease is smaller from 60 to 65 mph.

statement.p: Which of the following explains the meaning of the value of AV_{[60, 65]}\text{?}

li.p: AV_{[60, 65]} is the average amount of hours T has changed from 60 to 65 mph.
AV_{[60, 65]} is the average change in speed from 60 to 65 mph.
AV_{[60, 65]} is the average change in hours the trip takes for each one mph change in speed from 60 to 65 mph.
